title: Adaptive fragment buffering and TTL-based route steering for stable toolcall streams
author: Sofia Patel
commits: 4a1f8e6 - gateway: introduce adaptive fragment buffer with time-weighted smoothing
b7d3c21 - routing: add TTL-based route steering policy and metrics
d2f98b0 - compat: stabilize fncall frame sentinel and header parsing for OpenAI layer
c3e5a12 - docs: add streaming troubleshooting and rollout notes
e9a4f81 - tests: integration test for fragmented fncall streams
description: Motivation: Recent production incidents under mixed small/large payload workloads showed fragile fncall streaming in the OpenAI compatibility path: upstream clients would cut connections when interleaved small fragments triggered hard proxy buffers and route failovers. This PR implements two complementary mitigation strategies in the gateway surface: 1) an adaptive fragment buffering algorithm that smooths per-connection fragment pacing and avoids premature proxy drain/backpressure spikes, and 2) a TTL-based route steering policy that prefers low-latency route candidates for short-lived toolcall sessions while gently degrading to higher-capacity routes for long sessions. Summary of changes: - Adaptive fragment buffer (gateway/proxy/fragment_buffer.go): time-weighted fragment smoothing, max-burst caps, and a per-connection moving average used by the streaming writer to decide flush windows. Buffer behavior is controlled via feature flags and new helm values to allow staged rollout. - TTL-based route steering (gateway/routing/ttl_router.go): each request may carry an optional route_ttl hint (milliseconds); the router computes a preference score that decays as TTL approaches zero to avoid re-routing mid-stream. The router also exposes route.ttl_accepts and route.ttl_drops metrics. - OpenAI compat stabilization (gateway/proxy/protocol_compat.go): introduce a compact fncall frame header + newline sentinel for chunk boundaries to make the client-facing streaming protocol tolerant to fragment reassembly across the proxy buffer. This avoids mis-parsing when fragments are coalesced or split by intermediaries. - Observability (gateway/metrics/metrics_registry.go): new histograms and counters (gateway.stream.fragment_size_histogram, gateway.stream.fragment_flush_latency_ms, route.ttl_drops) and tagged dimensions for route and customer tier. - Tests and docs: integration test that simulates mixed-size fncall streams and a new docs page describing tuning knobs and rollback steps. Backwards compatibility: protocol changes are additive and backward tolerant; the compat layer falls back to legacy framing when strict compat=legacy is set. Rollout plan: staged canary behind feature flag: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 5 days with careful monitoring of fragment_flush_latency_ms and compat.fncall_frame_errors; automatic rollback threshold set for >3x error rate versus baseline. Performance: small overhead for light-weight smoothing (microseconds per fragment) but reduces spurious route failovers and decreases end-to-end toolcall tail latency on mixed workloads in our perf lab (p95 reduced by ~25% in fragbench). Related work: references ENG-4721 (streaming instability post-release) and ENG-4760 (gateway routing improvements); complements prior PRs on proxy chunk coalescing and credit decoupling. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for buffer logic - [x] Integration test for fncall framing - [x] Metrics emitted and wired to console dashboards - [x] Feature flag + helm knobs added - [x] Docs + runbook updated How tested: local unit test suite, fragbench micro-benchmarks, integration test harness that replays production capture for mixed-size requests, and a small internal canary. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and revert helm values; metrics and guards added to ensure quick detection of regressions.
review_comments: Initial review requested more explicit bounds on per-connection memory; responded by adding max-burst accounting and a hygiene unit test. Marcus asked for an audit of how TTL hints interact with canary routing; added guards so TTL is only advisory unless route_ttl_enforce is true for enterprise customers. Priya requested more metrics—added fragment_flush_latency_ms and compat.fncall_frame_errors. Lena recommended a tighter rollout (5% -> 25%); followed recommendation. Final approvals: Marcus (approve), Priya (approve), Lena (approve).
ci_details: CI: unit (pass), lint (pass), integration (flaky -> re-run passed), e2e perf (fragbench) run in separate job and passed against canary infra. One transient test failure in integration due to timing; re-run succeeded. All required checks green before merge.
release_notes:
- Gateway: add adaptive fragment buffering to smooth streaming fncall traffic and reduce spurious backpressure-induced route failovers.
- Gateway: introduce TTL-based route steering to prefer low-latency routes for short-lived toolcall sessions.
- OpenAI-compat: stabilize fncall framing with a compact header + sentinel to tolerate proxy fragment reassembly.
- Observability: new metrics for fragment sizes and flush latency.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag gateway.adaptive_frag_buffer=false by default in prod; roll out via canary gate. If increased fragment memory is observed, set gateway.frag.max_burst_bytes to 0 to disable burst. Watch metrics: gateway.stream.fragment_flush_latency_ms, compat.fncall_frame_errors, route.ttl_drops. If canary shows >3x frame errors, flip feature flag off and revert helm canary values.
